statement: MissionControl's public compatibility decoder distinguishes six motor-word layouts. Number bits from zero in a little-endian 32-bit word. The top two bits determine the main format: zero produces no samples; one selects one relative pair when bits 0–19 are zero, one absolute pair when bits 0–1 are zero otherwise, or three mixed samples otherwise; two selects two relative pairs when bits 0–9 are zero, or two mixed samples otherwise; three selects three relative pairs. For the pure relative layouts each pair occupies ten bits, earliest pair at bits 20–29, high-band command in its lower five bits and low-band command in its upper five bits. The conventional absolute pair has frequency/amplitude in bits 2–8/9–15 (high), 16–22/23–29 (low). Two mixed samples: bit 0 chooses the absolute band (1 high), bits 1–7 and 23–29 specify its frequency and amplitude, bits 18–22 specify the other band's first command, and the second high/low commands occupy bits 8–12/13–17. Three mixed samples: bit 0 chooses the band, bit 2 chooses frequency (1) or amplitude (0), bits 23–29 provide the first absolute index, bit 1 is documented as set, and the next two high/low command pairs occupy bits 13–17/18–22 and 3–7/8–12 respectively.

applicability.scope: Compatibility consumer layout only. Padding and ambiguous encodings are not established as valid device operations. The decoder's no-sample branch is not evidence of a physical stop. Each side has independent prior state.
